about.description:
GroundingDINO marries DINO with grounded pre-training for open-set object
detection: it detects objects named by a free-form text prompt rather than
by a fixed label set.

This feedstock publishes the project as several packages.  The Python is
identical across all of them; they differ only in whether the
`groundingdino._C` deformable-attention extension is present.  Without it
the model runs the pure-PyTorch implementation, which is correct but
substantially slower, and requires float32 -- `F.grid_sample` has no
half-precision CPU kernel.

tests.script: python -c "import groundingdino, pathlib, glob, sys; p = pathlib.Path(groundingdino.__file__).parent; assert glob.glob(str(p / '_C*.so')), 'the compiled extension is missing'"
python -c "import groundingdino, pathlib, glob, sys; p = pathlib.Path(groundingdino.__file__).parent; assert glob.glob(str(p / '_C*.so')), 'the compiled extension is missing'"

python -c "import groundingdino, pathlib, glob, sys; p = pathlib.Path(groundingdino.__file__).parent; assert glob.glob(str(p / '_C*.so')), 'the compiled extension is missing'"

name: groundingdino-py
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

# GroundingDINO, built as a multi-output recipe for rattler-build.
#
# The package splits along the one axis that actually exists in the source:
# whether the `groundingdino._C` deformable-attention extension is compiled.
#
#   groundingdino-py        the package.  Pure Python, no extension.  Imports
#                           fine everywhere; ms_deform_attn.py guards
#                           `from groundingdino import _C` in a try/except and
#                           falls back to multi_scale_deformable_attn_pytorch.
#   groundingdino-py-cuda   the CUDA-compiled `_C` alone, one file, depending on
#                           the package above.
#
# Two outputs, not four.  An earlier draft had a `-base` holding the Python with
# `groundingdino-py` an empty metapackage in front of it, plus a `-cpu`
# metapackage differing from that only by a constraint keeping `-cuda` out.
#
# Neither earned its place.  The indirection bought nothing that naming the
# Python package `groundingdino-py` does not, and `-cpu` guarded against
# something that cannot happen by accident: `-cuda` is opt-in, so nothing pulls
# it in unasked.  Not installing it is how you do not install it.
#
# There is deliberately no rocm or vulkan output.  See the note at the foot of
# this file: neither backend exists in the source to build against.

context:
  name: groundingdino-py
  version: "0.4.1"
  # Upstream's own tree, not the PyPI sdist.
  # The sdist ships no `csrc/`,
  # so the CUDA extension cannot be built from it at all --
  # which is why the primary package is pure Python
  # and why anyone wanting the compiled kernel has had to build it themselves.
  #
  # Upstream has cut no release since this commit;
  # it is `main` at the time of writing, pinned by hash.
  commit: 856dde20aee659246248e20734ef9ba5214f5e44
  # Architectures the extension is compiled for ahead of time.  conda-forge's
  # builders have no GPU, so nothing may depend on torch.cuda.is_available().
  cuda_arch_list: "8.0;8.6;8.9"

recipe:
  name: groundingdino-py-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO/archive/${{ commit }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 37b98b28341f95d1283631570c56b5ed3c92ea4af9717045f55f5045ca6fb2a0
    # Fixes submitted upstream and not yet merged.  Carried here rather than
    # waiting, because two of the three are load-bearing for this feedstock:
    # without 0002 the CUDA extension does not compile under CUDA 12 at all, and
    # without 0003 there is no version for packaging to read.  Drop each patch as
    # its pull request lands.
    #
    #   0001  IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO#458  transformers >= 4.49 compatibility
    #   0002  IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO#459  cuda_fp16.h include, fixes CUDA 12
    #   0003  IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO#460  __version__ attribute
    #   0004  IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO#462  Tensor::type() is deprecated and
    #                                          no longer converts, so the kernel
    #                                          does not compile under CUDA 12.9
    #
    # IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO#461 is deliberately *not* carried.  It extends
    # the SwinB config with training parameters, which is a proposal rather than
    # a fix, and no consumer of this package needs it: the configs are read from
    # disk by path, so a project wanting tuned ones ships its own.
    patches:
      - patches/0001-transformers-api-compat.patch
      - patches/0002-cuda-fp16-include.patch
      - patches/0003-version-attribute.patch
      - patches/0004-aten-deprecated-type.patch

build:
  # The recipe-wide build number.  Each output may override it; none do, so
  # bumping here bumps all of them together, which is what a rebuild against new
  # pinnings wants.
  number: 0

outputs:

  # ── Pure Python ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Everything except the compiled extension.  `noarch: python` is correct here
  # precisely because the arch-dependent part is factored into the cuda output.
  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}
      version: ${{ version }}

    build:
      noarch: python
      number: 0
      script:
        # No compiler and no TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST in this environment, so
        # setup.py's get_extensions() takes its else branch and returns None.
        # The wheel that results is pure Python -- which is what `noarch`
        # asserts, so the two have to stay in step.
        content:
          - python -m pip install . --no-deps --no-build-isolation -vv

    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools
        - wheel
        # setup.py does `import torch` at module level -- and, failing that,
        # tries to pip-install it, which cannot work in a sandboxed build.  It
        # is needed to read the metadata even though this output compiles
        # nothing.
        - pytorch >=2.1.0
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - pytorch >=2.1.0
        - torchvision
        - numpy >=1.26.2
        - opencv
        - supervision >=0.22.0
        - pycocotools
        - transformers >=4.49.0
        - addict
        - yapf
        - timm

    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - groundingdino
            - groundingdino.util.inference
          python_version: ${{ python_min }}.*
      - script:
          # The fallback is the contract of this output: importing the model
          # code must not require the extension.
          - python -c "from groundingdino.models.GroundingDINO.ms_deform_attn import multi_scale_deformable_attn_pytorch"

  # ── CUDA extension ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Ships only `groundingdino/_C*.so`; the Python lives in the base output.
  # Two packages may populate the same site-packages directory as long as they
  # do not claim the same file.
  - package:
      name: groundingdino-py-cuda
      version: ${{ version }}

    build:
      number: 0
      string: cuda${{ cuda_compiler_version | default("None") | replace(".", "") }}_py${{ python | replace(".", "") }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
      skip:
        # `undefined` and `"None"` both mean "no CUDA on this platform", and they
        # are not interchangeable: conda-forge's pinning omits the key entirely
        # for osx, so testing only against "None" lets the output through and the
        # template below fails during output discovery, before skip is consulted.
        - cuda_compiler_version is undefined or cuda_compiler_version == "None"
        - match(python, "<3.10")
      script:
        content:
          # CUDA_HOME has to be exported from the script rather than declared in
          # `env:` below, because only here does $BUILD_PREFIX expand.  It must
          # point at the prefix holding bin/nvcc: torch resolves its own
          # CUDA_HOME from this and silently falls back to a no-extension build
          # when it cannot find the compiler, which produces a py3-none-any
          # wheel rather than an error.
          - export CUDA_HOME="${BUILD_PREFIX}"
          - echo "CUDA_HOME=$CUDA_HOME"
          - ls -l "$CUDA_HOME/bin/nvcc"
          - python -c "import torch; print('torch', torch.__version__, 'built against CUDA', torch.version.cuda)"
          - python -c "from torch.utils.cpp_extension import CUDA_HOME; print('torch sees CUDA_HOME:', CUDA_HOME); assert CUDA_HOME, 'torch found no CUDA toolkit'"
          - python -m pip install . --no-deps --no-build-isolation -vv
          # Keep the extension, discard the Python that groundingdino-py-base
          # already owns.  Without this the two outputs collide on every .py.
          - python "$RECIPE_DIR/prune_to_extension.py" "$SP_DIR"
        env:
          # Compiled ahead of time.  setup.py takes its CUDA branch when
          # TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST is set even though no GPU is present, which is
          # what makes this buildable on GPU-less CI at all.
          FORCE_CUDA: "1"
          TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ cuda_arch_list }}

    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
        - ninja
      host:
        - python
        - pip
        - setuptools
        - wheel
        # The CUDA build specifically.  A CPU-built pytorch reports
        # torch.version.cuda == None, and torch then discards CUDA_HOME however
        # the environment is set -- so setup.py takes its no-extension branch
        # and quietly produces a py3-none-any wheel.
        - pytorch >=2.1.0 *cuda*
        - cuda-version ==${{ cuda_compiler_version | default("None") }}
        # torch's own CUDA headers include cusparse.h, cublas, cusolver and
        # curand transitively, so building any extension against them needs the
        # development packages present even though this kernel calls none of
        # them directly.  SelectiveTracking's pixi.toml had already accumulated
        # exactly this list.
        - cuda-cudart-dev
        - libcublas-dev
        - libcusparse-dev
        - libcusolver-dev
        - libcurand-dev
      run:
        - python
        - ${{ pin_subpackage(name, exact=False) }}
        - pytorch >=2.1.0 *cuda*
      run_constraints:
        - __cuda >=12.0

    tests:
      - script:
          # An import test would need a GPU; checking the object exists and
          # carries its entry points does not.
          - python -c "import groundingdino, pathlib, glob, sys; p = pathlib.Path(groundingdino.__file__).parent; assert glob.glob(str(p / '_C*.so')), 'the compiled extension is missing'"

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO
  summary: Open-set object detector
  description: |
    GroundingDINO marries DINO with grounded pre-training for open-set object
    detection: it detects objects named by a free-form text prompt rather than
    by a fixed label set.

    This feedstock publishes the project as several packages.  The Python is
    identical across all of them; they differ only in whether the
    `groundingdino._C` deformable-attention extension is present.  Without it
    the model runs the pure-PyTorch implementation, which is correct but
    substantially slower, and requires float32 -- `F.grid_sample` has no
    half-precision CPU kernel.
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file: LICENSE
  repository: https://github.com/IDEA-Research/GroundingDINO

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - giswqs
    - phreed

# ── Why there is no rocm or vulkan output ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# Both were considered and neither can be built from this source today.
#
# rocm:    the only HIP reference in the project is setup.py's non-CUDA branch,
#          which sets define_macros += [("WITH_HIP", None)] and then returns
#          None before the macro reaches a compiler -- so it is dead code, not a
#          backend.  csrc/ contains one CUDA kernel (ms_deform_attn_cuda.cu,
#          plus ms_deform_im2col_cuda.cuh) written against the CUDA runtime.
#          A rocm output needs that kernel hipified and a HIP build path added
#          to setup.py.  That is upstream work, and until it lands a rocm output
#          would ship the pure-Python fallback under a name promising otherwise.
#
# vulkan:  there is no Vulkan reference anywhere in the project, and PyTorch's
#          Vulkan backend does not support custom operators, so there is nothing
#          for a Vulkan output to compile.  An AMD or Intel GPU user is served
#          by groundingdino-py-cpu today.
#
